properties.global_prompt:
Photorealistic live-action biblical drama in natural afternoon light. The Temple opening is an earlier glimpse of the same young Judean man who later listens to Jesus on the hillside. Production role YOUNG LISTENER, identity YL-01: about twenty, clean-shaven, elongated oval face, warm brown skin, straight jet-black ear-length hair with a short fringe, ivory linen tunic, indigo mantle and brown belt pouch. Keep his same recognizable face, hair and clothes in the Temple, gateway and hillside. He is a real audience member in this film's framing story, entirely separate from the two brothers in Jesus's parable. His body language changes naturally with each action: relaxed upright posture in the Temple, torso and head facing his direction of travel at the gateway, and attentive seated posture on the hillside. Heads align naturally over shoulders. Frame featured characters from the waist up or closer. In broad ensemble compositions, foreground listeners naturally hide the featured characters below the waist while the crowd, architecture and landscape carry the scale. Preserve this framing throughout movement.
The hillside is one large gathering of roughly three hundred people arranged in irregular seated groups across the olive-covered slope. Jesus occupies the left third under the olive tree, with the crowd spreading behind him and across the right. YOUNG LISTENER sits in the lower-right foreground, beside a man in a brown headwrap on his screen-left. The religious leaders stand at the upper-right perimeter. The scribe is the older grey-bearded man at screen-left within their pair, in a dark brown outer robe and an ivory hood secured by a dark headband. The Pharisee is screen-right within their pair, with a long dark-and-salt-grey beard, cream outer robe and ivory head covering secured by a dark band. Preserve these heads, clothes and left-right positions in their close-ups. Preserve the large crowd scale in wide views, with nearer tax collectors and other listeners around Jesus. Small groups overlap in depth; gestures and reactions remain individual and restrained. Preserve the established Jesus face, hair, beard and clothing from the supplied images. Jesus begins seated, rises exactly once in segment 11, and remains standing afterward. Every segment is one continuous take with one modest, purposeful camera movement. Speaking faces stay large and sharp. Maintain consistent screen direction, daylight, location, clothing and character positions. Only the exact assigned dialogue is spoken once, with synchronized lips and natural breathing. Jesus retains one warm grounded adult male English voice. Temple chant, shofar and street sounds end at the location cut; hillside voices are local, quiet and limited to the assigned speaker or brief specified reaction. No invented foreground lines, narration or captions.
